Pairing t and −t with Jensen shows skew c cannot reduce any convex f(squared radius). For c=0, the rectangle integral is G_f=4∫0^a f(x²+b²)dx+4∫0^b f(y²+a²)dy; varying b at fixed a+b produces derivative 8ab∫0¹[f′(a²t²+b²)−f′(b²t²+a²)]dt≤0 for a>=b, with strictness for strictly convex C¹ f. Consequently equal-perimeter square is minimal in convex order, and E(r²)=L²/48 is constant. Power exponents p outside [0,2] minimize, inside maximize at square, with endpoints constant; boundaries exclude origin so p<0 finite. Exact quartic integration gives E4=L⁵/1280−LA²/12, explicitly known from earlier fourth-chord boundary m4 calculation. For shape-independent C² f, varying c and taking its second derivative at c=0, then b→0, yields ∫0^a z² f′′(z²)dz=0 for all a>0, hence f′′≡0; conversely affine f is invariant. Independently rationally integrated E2/E4 in representative orthogonal and skew systems and inspected symbolic verifier; these finite points corroborate, never prove, the convex-order functional inequality.
